issues.description: The selected revision carries forward CPU-specific paging requirements into newly generic paging proofs, so those proofs still exclude otherwise valid layouts.
issues.rationale: The trait contract requires every `C` to satisfy the architecture-global `PAGE_SIZE`, `NR_LEVELS`, and `NR_ENTRIES`, including `Self::NR_LEVELS() == 4` on x86. The x86 module then declares a lemma generic over any `C: PagingConstsTrait` and derives fixed 4-level/512-entry address constants from those requirements. A valid configuration with a different base page size, three levels, or a different PTE ratio is therefore excluded by the abstraction rather than handled by generic proofs. Both unresolved review threads identify this same root cause: the generic lemma's assumption is suspicious precisely because the trait contract smuggles hard-coded architecture constants into all implementations. The PR was closed without fixing it and explicitly superseded by #710. Follow-up diff check: the CPU-specific equalities predate this PR. This is a carried-forward defect in the selected review snapshot, not a claim that #532 first introduced those equalities. Its newly generic page_size and x86 proof surface continue to rely on that restriction; group with #530 for root-family-aware evaluation.
